references.authors: Braun JM, Smith KW, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Variability of urinary phthalate metabolite and bisphenol A concentrations before and during pregnancy
references.finding: During pregnancy ICCs were 0.50 for MEP, 0.45 for MBP, 0.25 for MBzP, 0.12 for BPA and 0.08 for sum-DEHP; one spot sample adequately classified MEP and MBP but not DEHP or BPA.

references.authors: Carwile JL, Ye X, Zhou X, et al.
references.title: Canned soup consumption and urinary bisphenol A: a randomized crossover trial
references.finding: One serving of canned soup a day for 5 days raised specific-gravity-adjusted urinary BPA to 20.8 ug/L vs 1.1 ug/L after fresh soup.

references.authors: Castellini C, Muselli M, Parisi A, et al.
references.title: Association between urinary bisphenol A concentrations and semen quality: A meta-analytic study
references.finding: Urinary BPA was only weakly associated with lower sperm motility, and the association disappeared after correction for publication bias; authors judge the link clinically negligible, if any.

references.authors: Ehrlich S, Calafat AM, Humblet O, et al.
references.title: Handling of thermal receipts as a source of exposure to bisphenol A
references.finding: Handling thermal receipts for 2 h without gloves raised urinary BPA from 1.8 to 5.8 ug/L, peaking at 8-12 h; nitrile gloves prevented a significant rise.

references.authors: Friedman A, Welch BM, Keil AP, et al.
references.title: Periods of susceptibility for associations between phthalate exposure and preterm birth: Results from a pooled analysis of 16 US cohorts
references.finding: In the same pooled data, DEHP-metabolite associations with preterm birth were strongest for first- and second-trimester exposure (MEHP OR 1.15 and 1.11 per IQR) and null in the third trimester.

references.authors: Génard-Walton M, Warembourg C, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Using mixture and exposome methods to assess the associations and interactions of chemical biomarkers with semen parameters
references.finding: Across four mixture/exposome models of 24 biomarkers (BPA, parabens, triclosan, 17 phthalate metabolites, hair mercury), the consistent signals were mercury (positive) and triclosan (negative); the overall mixture had small, imprecise associations with semen parameters.

references.authors: Goldstone AE, Chen Z, Perry MJ, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A and semen quality, the LIFE Study
references.finding: In a general-population preconception cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with 34 of 35 semen measures; the only significant finding was less sperm DNA fragmentation with higher BPA.

references.authors: Gougeon A
references.title: Dynamics of follicular growth in the human: a model from preliminary results
references.finding: The human ovulatory follicle begins its final growth about 85 days before ovulation; the dominant follicle is recruited 15-20 days before ovulation.

references.authors: Harley KG, Kogut K, Madrigal DS, et al.
references.title: Reducing Phthalate, Paraben, and Phenol Exposure from Personal Care Products in Adolescent Girls: Findings from the HERMOSA Intervention Study
references.finding: Three days of personal-care products free of phthalates, parabens, triclosan and BP-3 lowered urinary MEP by 27% and methyl/propyl paraben by about 44-45%; MnBP and MiBP did not change.

references.authors: Harray AJ, Lucas AD, Herrmann SE, et al.
references.title: Low-plastic diet and urinary levels of plastic-associated phthalates and bisphenols: the randomized controlled PERTH Trial
references.finding: A 7-day diet of food sourced to minimize plastic contact, with plastic-free kitchenware and personal-care products, cut urinary MnBP by 37.5%, MBzP by 53.5% and BPA by 59.7% vs no intervention; personal-care swaps alone lowered MnBP; Minderoo-funded.

references.authors: Hauser R, Gaskins AJ, Souter I, et al.
references.title: Urinary Phthalate Metabolite Concentrations and Reproductive Outcomes among Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilization: Results from the EARTH Study
references.finding: Women in the top vs bottom quartile of urinary DEHP metabolites had fewer and fewer mature oocytes and 19 percentage points lower clinical pregnancy and live birth per cycle.

references.authors: HELLER CG, CLERMONT Y
references.title: Spermatogenesis in man: an estimate of its duration
references.finding: One cycle of the human seminiferous epithelium lasts about 16 days and complete spermatogenesis about 64 days.

references.authors: Hormann AM, Vom Saal FS, Nagel SC, et al.
references.title: Holding thermal receipt paper and eating food after using hand sanitizer results in high serum bioactive and urine total levels of bisphenol A (BPA)
references.finding: Holding thermal receipt paper right after using a hand sanitizer with penetration enhancers, then eating fries by hand, raised serum unconjugated BPA to about 7 ng/mL within 90 min.

references.authors: Hunt PA, Koehler KE, Susiarjo M, et al.
references.title: Bisphenol a exposure causes meiotic aneuploidy in the female mouse
references.finding: Accidental and then deliberate low-dose BPA exposure during the final stages of oocyte growth caused dose-dependent meiotic aneuploidy in female mice.

references.authors: Johns LE, Cooper GS, Galizia A, et al.
references.title: Exposure assessment issues in epidemiology studies of phthalates
references.finding: Phthalate metabolite half-lives are 3-18 h; intraclass correlations of repeated urine samples are about 0.3-0.6 for DEP, DBP, DiBP and BBzP metabolites and 0.1-0.3 for DEHP, DiNP and DiDP; US and German exposures to DEP, BBzP, DBP and DEHP declined after 2001.

references.authors: Koch HM, Bolt HM, Angerer J
references.title: Di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate (DEHP) metabolites in human urine and serum after a single oral dose of deuterium-labelled DEHP
references.finding: After a labelled DEHP dose, urinary metabolites peaked at 2-4 h; first-phase excretion half-lives were about 2 h and second-phase 5-10 h.

references.authors: Lessmann F, Schütze A, Weiss T, et al.
references.title: Metabolism and urinary excretion kinetics of di(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate (DEHTP) in three male volunteers after oral dosage
references.finding: After an oral DEHTP dose about 16% was recovered as specific metabolites, 95% of it within the first 24 h; 5cx-MEPTP was the main biomarker.

references.authors: Machtinger R, Gaskins AJ, Racowsky C, et al.
references.title: Urinary concentrations of biomarkers of phthalates and phthalate alternatives and IVF outcomes
references.finding: Higher DEHP metabolites were linked to fewer total, mature and fertilized oocytes and top-quality embryos, but no phthalate metabolite was linked to implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth; DINCH metabolites showed no associations.

references.authors: Mínguez-Alarcón L, Gaskins AJ, Chiu YH, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and association with in vitro fertilization outcomes among women from a fertility clinic
references.finding: In the expanded Boston cohort, urinary BPA was not associated with peak estradiol, fertilization, embryo quality, implantation, clinical pregnancy or live birth.

references.authors: Mok-Lin E, Ehrlich S, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Urinary bisphenol A concentrations and ovarian response among women undergoing IVF
references.finding: Each log-unit increase in urinary BPA was associated with 12% fewer oocytes retrieved and 213 pg/mL lower peak estradiol.

references.authors: Oh J, Choi JW, Ahn YA, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol S in humans after single oral administration
references.finding: Oral BPS was absorbed within about 1 h and excreted with a terminal half-life under 7 h (6.8 h).

references.authors: Pacchierotti F, Ranaldi R, Eichenlaub-Ritter U, et al.
references.title: Evaluation of aneugenic effects of bisphenol A in somatic and germ cells of the mouse
references.finding: Single, 7-day or 7-week oral BPA exposure did not induce hyperploidy or polyploidy in mouse oocytes or zygotes; only prematurely separated chromatids after chronic exposure, without effect on segregation.

references.authors: Peng CY, Tsai EM, Kao TH, et al.
references.title: Canned food intake and urinary bisphenol a concentrations: a randomized crossover intervention study
references.finding: A canned-food meal raised urinary BPA by up to 206% at 4 h, returning to baseline by 24 h.

references.authors: Rudel RA, Gray JM, Engel CL, et al.
references.title: Food packaging and bisphenol A and bis(2-ethyhexyl) phthalate exposure: findings from a dietary intervention
references.finding: Three days of fresh, unpackaged food cut urinary BPA by 66% and DEHP metabolites by 53-56% (geometric means).

references.authors: Sathyanarayana S, Alcedo G, Saelens BE, et al.
references.title: Unexpected results in a randomized dietary trial to reduce phthalate and bisphenol A exposures
references.finding: A 5-day catered 'low-exposure' diet unexpectedly raised urinary DEHP metabolites (to an estimated intake above EPA and EFSA limits for children) because ingredients such as ground coriander and milk were contaminated.

references.authors: Stahlhut RW, Welshons WV, Swan SH
references.title: Bisphenol A data in NHANES suggest longer than expected half-life, substantial nonfood exposure, or both
references.finding: Urinary BPA barely fell with longer fasting (population-based half-life 43 h), suggesting substantial non-food exposure, storage, or both.

references.authors: Teeguarden JG, Calafat AM, Ye X, et al.
references.title: Twenty-four hour human urine and serum profiles of bisphenol a during high-dietary exposure
references.finding: During three high-BPA meals, urinary total BPA peaked about 2.75 h after a meal; serum BPA was detectable only at exposures well above the US 95th percentile.

references.authors: Thayer KA, Doerge DR, Hunt D, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of bisphenol A in humans following a single oral administration
references.finding: After an oral dose of deuterated BPA, unconjugated BPA peaked at 1.3 h and the terminal half-life of total and unconjugated BPA was about 6.2-6.4 h.

references.authors: Vernet C, Philippat C, Agier L, et al.
references.title: An Empirical Validation of the Within-subject Biospecimens Pooling Approach to Minimize Exposure Misclassification in Biomarker-based Studies
references.n: 16 pregnant women (all voids, several weeks) plus simulation
references.finding: One spot urine sample produced 69% attenuation bias in a BPA dose-response; about 18 samples were needed to bring bias down to 10%.

references.authors: Wang H, He H, Wei Y, et al.
references.title: Do phthalates and their metabolites cause poor semen quality? A systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies on risk of decline in sperm quality
references.finding: Urinary MBP (pooled OR 2.19) and MBzP (OR 1.88) and semen DEHP (r -0.23) were associated with low sperm concentration; no significant links with motility or morphology or for MEP and other metabolites.

references.authors: Yland JJ, Zhang Y, Williams PL, et al.
references.title: Phthalate and DINCH urinary concentrations across pregnancy and risk of preterm birth
references.finding: Mean pregnancy sum-DEHP was imprecisely linked to preterm birth (RR 1.21, 0.84-1.72 per ln unit), with the clearest signal in the third trimester (RR 1.51); detection of a DINCH metabolite also appeared positively related to preterm birth.

timing.summary: Phthalates are cleared in hours, so urine reflects roughly the last day and a change of food or toiletries shows up within 3-7 days [ept-koch2004, ept-rudel2011, ept-harray2026]. The flip side is that the benefit lasts only while the change is kept up, and a single urine sample says little about the previous months [ept-johns2015].

onset.text: After a DEHP dose, urinary metabolites peak at 2-4 hours [ept-koch2004]. Reductions are equally fast: 3 days of fresh food cut DEHP metabolites 53-56% [ept-rudel2011], 3 days of fragrance-free products cut MEP 27% [ept-harley2016], and 7 days of low-plastic food cut MnBP 37.5% and MBzP 53.5% [ept-harray2026].

full.text: Urine reaches its new level within about 3-7 days of a sustained change [ept-rudel2011, ept-harray2026]; nothing builds beyond that.

after_stopping.text: Metabolite half-lives are about 2 hours in a first phase and 5-10 hours in a second phase for DEHP [ept-koch2004], 3-18 hours across phthalates [ept-johns2015]; DEHTP is 95% excreted within 24 hours [ept-lessmann2016]. Levels return to the old baseline within a day or two of going back to the old habits.

frequency.text: Because exposure is cleared in hours, avoidance protects only on the days it is practised; there is no carry-over [ept-johns2015]. Even careful diets can be undone by contaminated ingredients [ept-sathyanarayana2013].

timing.debate: Kinetics are not disputed, but their meaning for health studies is: because a spot urine has an ICC of only 0.08-0.3 for DEHP [ept-braun2012, ept-johns2015], studies of long-term outcomes are badly misclassified, and the pooled preterm-birth data put the sensitive window in early pregnancy [ept-friedman2025] while a fertility cohort found it in late pregnancy [ept-yland2022].

sperm.late_start: Starting 2-4 weeks before still lowers exposure within days [ept-rudel2011], but covers only the last stages of sperm maturation; no trial shows any semen benefit at any lead time.
sperm.text: The 64-day spermatogenic cycle plus epididymal transit sets the lead time [ept-heller1963], not the chemistry, which clears in a day [ept-koch2004].

egg.late_start: Starting in the last 2-4 weeks still lowers exposure during dominant-follicle selection and the treatment cycle, which is when the IVF studies measured it [ept-hauser2016]; it cannot cover earlier follicle growth.
egg.text: Lead time follows the ~85-day follicle growth period [ept-gougeon1986]; for pregnancy, pooled data point to the first and second trimesters for DEHP [ept-friedman2025].

timing.summary: BPA and BPS have half-lives of about 6-7 hours [ept-thayer2015, ept-oh2018], so a canned meal shows up within hours and is gone in a day [ept-peng2019]. Receipts are slower: skin uptake peaks 8-12 hours after handling and is still raised at 24 hours [ept-ehrlich2014].

onset.text: Urinary BPA peaks about 2.75-4 hours after a BPA-containing meal [ept-teeguarden2011, ept-peng2019] and 8-12 hours after handling receipts [ept-ehrlich2014]. A fresh-food diet cut urinary BPA 66% in 3 days [ept-rudel2011] and a low-plastic diet 60% in 7 days [ept-harray2026].

full.text: The new level is reached within about 1-7 days [ept-rudel2011, ept-harray2026].

after_stopping.text: Terminal half-life of unconjugated BPA about 6.2 hours [ept-thayer2015], BPS 6.8 hours [ept-oh2018]; canned-meal BPA was back to baseline by 24 hours [ept-peng2019].

frequency.text: Every canned or plastic-packaged meal re-exposes you [ept-carwile2011, ept-peng2019]; avoidance works only while maintained. Because one urine sample captures a single day, about 18 samples were needed to rank a person's average BPA exposure well [ept-vernet2019].

timing.debate: Dosing studies give a half-life of about 6 hours [ept-thayer2015, ept-teeguarden2011], but NHANES urinary BPA barely fell with fasting, implying an apparent population half-life of 43 hours from non-food sources or storage [ept-stahlhut2009]; dermal routes (receipts, especially after hand sanitizer) are slower than oral ones [ept-ehrlich2014, ept-hormann2014].

sperm.late_start: A late start lowers current exposure within days but covers only the final maturation of sperm already in production.
sperm.text: Lead time set by the 64-day cycle plus epididymal transit [ept-heller1963]; semen associations themselves are inconsistent [ept-castellini2022, ept-goldstone2015].

egg.late_start: If the mouse data apply, the final 2-4 weeks (dominant follicle and meiotic resumption) are the most important to cover, so a late start is not wasted [ept-hunt2003, ept-gougeon1986].
egg.text: About 85 days of follicle growth set the full lead time [ept-gougeon1986]; the meiotic window is the last part of it [ept-hunt2003].
